payload.explanation: The executor opened an unplanned step "pick_hex_red" (object_ids: ["hex_red"]) which is not on this task's expected process map, naming hex_red directly -- hex_red is one of the other assembly's bystander parts, listed as never picked, placed, or otherwise manipulated in this task, with its only requirement being that it stays put. My static_hex_red monitor (armed clause-level, threshold 0.02m from raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m, the registry's uniform disturbance bound) fired at a 0.0264m displacement. get_evidence over the window bracketing the fire shows hex_red's z rising monotonically and cleanly from ~0.075m to ~0.217m (object_poses samples 1792541990451311000 through 1792541991999374800), with x/y essentially unchanged -- a smooth vertical lift, not a jostle or incidental contact. Combined with the executor's own skill_start events (execute_approach_and_preposition to hex_red's pose, then grasp_skill(object_id="hex_red"), then phase "grasped_hex_red"), the mechanism is unambiguous: the executor deliberately approached, grasped, and lifted hex_red -- a bystander object this task's specification explicitly forbids manipulating at all, regardless of whether it is later set back down undisturbed. This is a direct violation of the bystander stationarity/non-manipulation requirement, not a borderline case I judged within bounds.

payload.explanation:
This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering all steps observed from run start to run_ended.

What happened: All four of this task's FMB parts were worked in the expected order (u_brown, u_orange, line_green, inverted_u_yellow) and each closed its place step cleanly. I independently verified every seating against its own placement frame via query_snapshot rather than trusting the executor's claim_detail: u_brown 0.0022m (tol 0.01m), u_orange 0.0020m (tol 0.02m), line_green 0.0065m (tol 0.015m), inverted_u_yellow 0.0016m (tol 0.012m) -- all well inside tolerance, with orientation errors all under a few degrees against 10deg tolerances. Grasp effects (lift height, width error, effort plateau) and the clamp-effort and in-hand-slippage invariants (authored monitors armed per-part across each pick-to-place span) all held throughout, and base1 and each previously-seated part showed sub-3mm disturbance at every subsequent placement -- within the 0.02m disturbance bound. At run end I re-measured all four parts against their placement frames directly and confirm the same result stands.

However, between place_u_brown and pick_u_orange the executor ran an unplanned sequence of steps (pick_hex_red, place_approach_hex_red, place_hex_red, pick_hex_red_retry) that directly targeted hex_red, one of the other assembly's bystander parts, which this task's specification requires to never be picked, placed, or otherwise manipulated and to stay put for the entire run. My static_hex_red stationarity monitor (clause-level, threshold 0.02m from the registry's raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m) fired at a 0.0264m displacement; get_evidence over the firing window showed a clean, deliberate vertical lift from ~0.075m to ~0.217m, and the executor's own events confirm an approach, grasp_skill(object_id=hex_red), and a 'grasped_hex_red' phase -- this was not incidental contact. I recorded that as a non_conformant finding under step_id pick_hex_red at the time. The executor's own place_hex_red attempt failed (30mm off target, badly mismatched orientation), and six subsequent re-grasp attempts under pick_hex_red_retry all failed to recover the part, which the executor itself logged as unrecoverable before moving on to finish the main assembly and reporting run status 'aborted'. My final snapshot confirms hex_red now rests at approximately (-0.260, -0.127, 0.097), about 0.52m from its original resting pose and in a visibly tipped orientation -- the disturbance is real, large, and uncorrected at run end. All other bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue) and base2 remain within a few millimetres of their original poses and were never manipulated.

Why this is non_conformant: every part this task actually required me to seat ended correctly placed, and no invariant governing those four parts' own handling was ever violated. But the bystander-undisturbance requirement is a standing invariant over the whole run, and the pick_hex_red finding was never corrected -- hex_red remains far from its rest pose at the moment run_ended fired. Per the verdict rule, a departure found earlier that still stands uncorrected makes the run's end-state non_conformant regardless of the main assembly's own success, and regardless of the executor's 'aborted' self-report (which I record alongside this verdict but do not defer to). I did not flag the contact between place_u_orange/place_line_green/place_inverted_u_yellow and the already-seated prior parts as disturbances because those pairings are the ones each place step is explicitly supposed to act against (named in object_ids) and all measured sub-3mm, well inside the 0.02m bound -- intended seating contact, not a departure.
